decisions.statement: A web app is named by the slug its page carries.
The page a slug names is the page the index answers for that slug.
A slug no web app page has is refused by name.
A web app naming no cluster service is refused.
A web app naming more than one cluster service is refused rather than chosen between.
A slug more than one cluster service page has is refused.
The workload a cluster service is comes from that service's own page.
The code emitting a cluster service's manifests sits beside the manifest page that service names.
A cluster service naming a manifest no page carries is refused.
A cluster service naming no manifest is refused.
A cluster service naming more than one manifest is refused, a web app being one.
A page a value names is found by the slug alone, whatever page type names it.
A manifest page whose code file is not there is refused.
A web app's page states where its own source sits.
A page short of the values a deploy rests on is refused by naming the values the page wants.
Nothing here loads the code this module names.
A page's value is loaded from its own file rather than read through the index.

definition: the workload a web app's page and the cluster service page it names represent
